q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of peanut butter per kg?
title: Peanut butter carbon footprint per kg
short: Groundnuts are the main input: multiply the kernels per kg by the supplier's figure. Add roasting, blanching, grinding and filling energy and the jars, then divide the plant's energy by kg packed.
audience: Peanut butter and nut spread makers

ul: PET or glass jars with caps.
Roasting with gas or electric roasters.

p: Report per kg with the pack shown separately, since a glass jar weighs far more than PET.

example.title: Worked example: peanut butter unit per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 8,730 / 60,000 = 0.145 kg CO2 per kg
Add groundnuts and jars for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
